text:
Ryan sent me a message at midnight, desiring to speak with me; and I knew at once what such a request implied.

We met on the following day at the place appointed, where he was before me, and looked very much discomposed; he said he was not ready for any thing so serious, and the fault, he assured me, was not mine but his own.

I wished to cry, but did not; I only nodded, and said it was all right, and then walked home in the rain, and consoled myself with a great deal of ice.

My friend, who shared my lodgings, thought me too much affected; I was not unwilling to allow she might be right, but it hurt me still.

I just nodded and said okay.
Then I walked home in the rain and ate a whole pint of ice cream.

explanation: Fourteen short sentences are gathered into four periods joined by semicolons and commas; the contractions, the telephone, and the modern places and words give way to plain equivalents; feeling is shown by conduct, and the concession to the friend is made by understatement.

notes.austen: “No, but I wrote to him—I did indeed, I got up this morning before it was light, and was two hours about it; and when my letter was done I thought I never should have courage to give it.

notes.austen: Now, as we may fairly suppose, he would not allow much time to pass before he spoke to the lady, and as he does not appear to have spoken yesterday, it is not unlikely that he should be at Mrs. Goddard’s today; and she may be detained by a visitor, without thinking him at all a tiresome wretch.”
